title: Sticky BBQ Chicken Wings
changes_from_base: Same baking-powder oven method as the Classic wings, with smoked paprika in the coating. The baked wings are tossed in a warm, tangy BBQ-honey glaze and topped with spring onion.
summary: These wings follow the same baking-powder base method as the classic recipe with smoked paprika added, then get tossed in a warm, tangy BBQ-honey glaze and topped with spring onion.
equipment: 2 wire racks that fit the trays

ingredients.item: chicken wings, split into drumettes and flats
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Dry and season
steps.text: Pat the split wings dry, then toss with the baking powder, salt, pepper and smoked paprika in a large bowl, following the same base method as the classic oven wings. The baking powder raises the skin's pH to help it blister and brown; always use baking powder here, never bicarbonate of soda, which tastes soapy.

steps.title: Arrange on racks
steps.text: Lay the wings skin-side up on wire racks over two trays, spaced apart. Refrigerating uncovered for 1 hour up to overnight dries the skin further, though this step can be skipped if pressed for time. Switch the oven on to 120°C (100°C fan) roughly 20 minutes ahead, setting shelves in the lower-middle and upper-middle positions.

steps.title: Render at low heat
steps.text: Bake at 120°C (100°C fan) on the lower-middle shelves for 30 minutes to render out the fat gently. This keeps the skin from browning too fast before the fat underneath has had a chance to melt away.

steps.title: Blast at high heat
steps.text: Raise the oven to 220°C (200°C fan) and bake for 40-50 minutes, swapping the trays halfway through. Continue until deep golden and blistered, with the thickest drumette at least 74°C - pushing to 80°C or above gives a more tender result.

steps.title: Make the glaze
steps.text: While the wings bake, simmer the barbecue sauce, honey, cider vinegar and cayenne pepper together in a small saucepan for 2-3 minutes until slightly thickened. Simmering concentrates the glaze a little so it clings to the wings rather than running straight off.

steps.title: Toss in the glaze
steps.text: Rest the baked wings for 5 minutes, then tip them into a big bowl with the warm glaze and toss until every piece is coated and sticky. Adding the glaze after baking rather than in the oven means the sugars can't scorch on the hot trays.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Scatter over the sliced spring onions and serve while still warm, with plenty of napkins. The crisp skin underneath holds the glaze without going soggy if you eat them soon after tossing.

tips: Toss the wings in the glaze only after they come out of the oven, and serve soon. Don't brush glaze on in the oven, because the honey and sauce sugars burn within a minute or two at 220°C.
For the crispiest skin, leave the seasoned wings uncovered on their racks in the fridge overnight before baking.
Simmer the glaze until just slightly thickened, not syrupy, so it coats the wings rather than clumping.
Bottled barbecue sauces vary: check the label for gluten (malt vinegar or Worcestershire sauce) and allergens such as mustard, celery or fish before you buy.
storage: Keep glazed wings in the fridge for up to 3 days; freezing isn't recommended once sauced, as the glaze can turn watery on thawing. Reheat in a hot oven until piping hot and 74°C in the centre. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
